title: Silvercrest Finance - Onprem airgapped discovery
summary: Discovery call for on-prem, air-gapped deployment for regulated finance workloads. Customer runs strict data residency and offline update policies, wants details on networking, hardware, HSM/KMS, offline model updates, and pilot/POC scope. AE+SE to share security pack, propose bench, and draft SOW for pilot.
topics: hardware constraints (H100 vs A100, GPU counts)
action_items: Jordan (AE) - send security whitepaper, SOC2 summary, and architecture checklist - due 2026-06-24
Priya (SE) - schedule benchmark run and provide benchmark plan (latency/throughput tests) - due 2026-06-26
Maya (Customer) - share hardware inventory and rack/network constraints (GPU types, firmware) - due 2026-06-22
Samir (Customer) - confirm legal/security contact for encryption/KMS questions - due 2026-06-20
next_steps: Share security docs + SOC2 + onprem install guide (Jordan)
Run bench in lab with customer's hardware profile (Priya)
Schedule technical deep-dive with infra & security (week of 2026-06-22)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-17 16:00 UTC | Duration: 53m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (CTO), Maya (Head of Infra), Samir (Security), Lena (ML Platform)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood. Quick intros, and Priya's our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Evan: Hey yeah Evan here, CTO at Silvercrest. We run the ML infra team.
[00:15] Maya: Maya - infra. We're the folks who will have to actually host this.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, security lead. My main concern is air-gap and key custody.
[00:25] Jordan: Great. Today we want to understand your constraints — air-gapped onprem, what success looks like, perf targets, and then next steps for a pilot.
[00:35] Priya: Hi — quick note, from Redwood side we support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (on-prem). For air-gapped we typically do our Redwood Private package with offline installers + a customer-managed control plane.
[00:48] Maya: When you say offline installers, can you clarify? We cannot have any outbound egress from the inference racks.
[00:55] Priya: Yeah that's common. We provide an installer tarball plus a signed package you can ingest via internal blob storage. All images are signed, we support detached signatures for verification, and we can do image manifests that you validate with your own sigtool.
[01:12] Lena: How do you handle model updates? Our compliance team requires changelogs and offline validation before any model crosses the air-gap.
[01:20] Jordan: We have two flows — scheduled offline update (you pull the artifact, run validation harness, then apply) or an internal-only sync via a secure file transfer. We'll provide checksums and a signed release manifest. Priya, you want to add on the validation harness?
[01:36] Priya: Sure. We can include an eval harness that runs locally with a defined prompt set; it outputs metric diffs and an approval token. That way legal/security can verify before deployment.
[01:46] Samir: We need the crypto side explained — KMS, HSM. We can't have keys leaving our H S M. Does Redwood support customer-managed K M S or H S M integration?
[01:56] Priya: Yes — K M S integration is supported. For air-gapped we mount an internal K M S or H S M. We don't require keys to leave your network. Our runtime can be configured to call your H S M over internal LAN or use a local key agent.
[02:10] Maya: OK. Latency targets — we have trading/near-real-time risk scoring. Need sub-100ms for short prompts at 512 tokens and 200 req/s on peak. Is that realistic on on-prem?
[02:24] Priya: Depends on hardware. For sub-100ms at that QPS, you'd likely want H100s or very optimized A100 setups with NVLink. Also model choice matters — smaller quantized models or trimmed context. We can advise on quantization profiles and batching.
[02:41] Evan: We currently have an inventory of 8x A100 80GB per rack and two racks available, but we might be limited on PCIe fabric.
[02:50] Priya: That could work. We'll need to see the PCIe/NVLink topology. If you can't do NVLink across all GPUs, throughput and KV cache sharing will be impacted for large context models.
[03:05] Guest (SRE): Our firmware is older on some nodes, do you require specific driver versions?
[03:09] Priya: We publish supported driver/OS matrix. Usually NVIDIA driver 535+ for A100/H100; CUDA toolkit compatible versions. We can run a preflight script to validate.
[03:18] Jordan: Let's talk about networking. You mentioned no egress; how do you want health checks and telemetry handled?
[03:25] Samir: No telemetry offsite by default. We'll allow a telemetry sink to a customer-managed logging cluster that Redwood can query over a VPN if necessary, but only read-only and restricted.
[03:36] Priya: Our console is optional. For Private deployments we can ship with console disabled; you can enable a read-only metrics endpoint that forwards to your internal Prometheus/ELK.
[03:47] Lena: For the evals, can Redwood reproduce perf numbers we see in the field? We need deterministic benchmarking for procurement.
[03:54] Priya: We'll provide a benchmark harness and can run it in your lab. It measures p95 latency, tail, throughput, token cost and memory. We also provide model variants that are quantized. Note: quantization can change quality — we'll include eval diffs.
[04:10] Evan: About licensing and pricing — what's the model for Private on-prem? Fixed seat vs throughput?
[04:15] Jordan: For Private we usually do a fixed platform fee plus support tiers, and an optional reserved capacity component if you want dedicated throughput guarantees. For pilots we'd propose a short-term pilot license and then scale to committed capacity. We'll send a draft S O W.
[04:28] Maya: Support window — do you offer 24/7 SRE during on-call or only business hours?
[04:33] Jordan: Enterprise support offers 24/7 pager coverage for critical incidents. Can include field support for install at additional cost.
[04:41] Samir: Audit logs — do you provide native audit logs for model calls and admin actions? We need tamper-evident logs for compliance.
[04:50] Priya: Yes, the runtime emits audit logs and we can integrate with your SIEM. For air-gapped we'll write to an append-only store or forward to your internal SIEM. We can also support signing logs with a key to be tamper-evident.
[05:05] Jordan: Anything else about data residency or retention?
[05:09] Samir: All PII must be redacted by default, and retention policies enforced. We can't have logs older than X stored offsite — everything stays internal unless expressly exported.
[05:20] Priya: We'll include configurable retention policies and redaction hooks. Our streaming path can be configured to not persist request bodies by default.
[05:30] Evan: On the model side, do you support bringing our own models (BYOM)? We have a customized risk model.
[05:36] Priya: Yes, BYOM is supported. For air-gapped, you package the model artifact and we onboard it via the offline flow. We'll provide model packaging guidance and quantization suggestions.
[05:47] Lena: How about model provenance and reproducibility? We need an immutable record of which model version served traffic and when.
[05:53] Priya: The runtime stamps every deployment with a manifest and unique release ID, which is logged in audit trails. For each request you can map back to a model release ID.
[06:03] Jordan: On the POC — what would success criteria look like for you?
[06:08] Evan: For us it's two things: 1) match latency SLOs for a subset of inference templates, and 2) ensure security/compliance checks pass (K M S, offline updates). If both good, we move to a 3-month pilot.
[06:20] Maya: Also must fit in a single rack deployment initially. We won't commit more hardware until we see bench results.
[06:26] Priya: Understood. We'll propose a bench that runs on your single-rack profile.
[06:30] Jordan: Let's go deeper on hardware specifics — Priya, can you give an example config that meets their 200 rps sub-100ms target?
[06:38] Priya: Example: 4x H100 80GB with full NVLink and optimized kernel set, or 8x A100 80GB with NVSwitch in a single rack. Use smaller quantized model if possible. We also recommend enabling KV cache pinning and continuous batching tuned to 10-20 ms windows.
[06:55] Samir: What about failover? If a node goes down do you have graceful degradation and model fallback?
[07:01] Priya: Yes — routing policies allow fallback to a smaller model or to a dedicated capacity pool if available. In onprem-only setups you can configure degraded routing to a smaller local model.
[07:10] Evan: The procurement team will ask about maintenance windows. How are updates scheduled?
[07:15] Jordan: Updates are scheduled by you — we provide signed release artifacts and an approval token generated by your validation harness.
[07:22] Guest (SRE): Do you require outbound to check licenses?
[07:25] Priya: No for air-gapped. License checks can be done offline via signed entitlements.
[07:30] Samir: Are there any third-party dependencies that require internet access?
[07:33] Priya: Only optional telemetry/auto-updates. Core runtime and model artifacts can be fully offline. We'll supply all dependencies in the installer bundle.
[07:42] Evan: Let's talk about timeline. If we agree to a pilot, how quickly can you get us a bundle and a bench plan?
[07:49] Jordan: We can produce a pilot S O W and security pack within a week. Bench plan from SE in two weeks. Onsite install typically 4-8 weeks depending on procurement.
[08:00] Lena: For the bench, can you simulate production traffic patterns? We have spiky bursts during market open.
[08:07] Priya: Yes — our harness supports bursty traffic patterns, open-loop and closed-loop tests, and tail-latency reporting.
[08:15] Maya: Any special rack power or cooling requirements we should consider?
[08:20] Priya: Power density and cooling guidance depends on GPU mix. We'll include rack-level power draw estimates in the installer docs.
[08:26] Evan: About legal: export controls, we operate in multiple jurisdictions. Any limitations?
[08:31] Jordan: We'll surface export control guidance in the S O W. For some models there are export restrictions; we can provide model variants that are compliant.
[08:39] Samir: On logging, can we retain the logs for 7 years if needed? Compliance requires long retention but offline archiving might be needed.
[08:46] Priya: You can set retention to any policy; for long-term cold storage we recommend an internal archive that the runtime can push to on schedule.
[08:55] Jordan: Quick check — any blockers today to moving forward with a pilot?
[08:58] Maya: We need to confirm hardware compatibility and the PCIe/NVLink topology. Also need legal to review security docs.
[09:06] Evan: Procurement will need licensing and price ranges.
[09:09] Jordan: We'll send a ballpark pricing for pilot plus the S O W.
[09:14] Priya: I'll put together benchmark plan with clear artifacts we'll need from you.
[09:19] Samir: Also please include H S M integration notes; we run Thales and a cloud H S M for some environments.
[09:27] Priya: Noted. We support Thales and other H S M vendors; we'll document the integration steps.
[09:34] Jordan: Ok let's do a rapid recap and next steps.
[09:37] Jordan: Action items - Jordan to send security pack and S O W, Priya to send bench plan, Maya to share hardware inventory, Samir to identify legal contact.
[09:48] Evan: Sounds good. One more — can Redwood do a short internal training for our SREs on day of install?
[09:54] Jordan: Yes, we offer install training as part of the pilot — remote or onsite. We'll include an estimate.
[09:59] Lena: Thanks all.
[10:02] End of meeting.
